slides.say: Debouncing waits for the user to stop typing. Throttling updates at most once in a while. Use deferred value works differently.

slides.text: No fixed delay: on a fast device it updates almost instantly; on a slow one it lags just enough.
slides.say: It needs no fixed delay. On a fast laptop, the deferred render happens almost immediately. On a slow phone, it lags in proportion to the device.

slides.text: Interruptible: a new keystroke abandons the background render. Debounce still blocks later.
slides.say: And it is interruptible. A new keystroke abandons the background render. Debouncing only postpones the moment the render blocks typing.

slides.text: Fewer network requests? Debounce still helps. You can combine them.
slides.say: Debouncing is still useful for work outside rendering, like firing fewer network requests. You can use both together.
